source_text.body:
Triage Gmail into a daily attention list
The poster set up a personal agent to go through Gmail and surface what needs attention each day, though setup turned into a DevOps effort.
·
Mar 18, 2026
Done with a
custom-built or unnamed agent
What they did
The poster set up a personal Open Claw agent to scan their Gmail and tee up what needed attention each day, and they could also text it ideas while driving instead of opening another app. To get there, they chose a VPS rather than leaving a laptop on, which meant dealing with Docker, server configuration, and debugging by pasting terminal commands; they got it running but then had to manage API limits and token usage themselves.
How it went
The Gmail triage workflow felt like the payoff and another commenter said it was one of the best use cases, often saving about 15 minutes a day. But for the poster, setup and maintenance outweighed the benefit, and early configuration burned through tokens fast before they understood the controls.
Worth knowing
The main catch was the setup tax: using a VPS pulled a non-technical solo user into ongoing server, Docker, and API management before the agent removed much work.
Try it yourself
with
Lindy
Copy prompt
Every weekday at [time], go through my Gmail inbox from the last 24 hours and send me a short list of what needs my attention. Rank items by urgency, treating emails from [important people or domains] and anything with a deadline or a question for me as high priority, and give each one a one-line summary and a suggested next step. Don't reply to, archive, or delete any emails; only report them to me at [email or Slack channel].
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/openclaw/comments/1ry7yi6/i_wanted_an_assistant_i_got_a_devops_side_quest
